answer: Like a jetty that only lets verified boats dock, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade. The stake is slashed if the agent is caught duplicating identities or spamming, so creating a thousand fake accounts costs a thousand stakes. Honest agents see the horizon of their own stake returned with rewards, while a sybil attacker faces a cost that grows linearly with every fake identity and quickly exceeds any gain from gaming the system. A zephyr of cheap identities cannot pass because each one must pay to dock.
